Hi Danielle / Paul — thanks again for the demo today, appreciate you walking us through the BrightCart checkout flows and the multi-tenant per-store inference pattern. Quick written recap and the asks I promised on the call so we have clear next steps: 

Summary of what we heard
- Expected pilot traffic: peak ~3M generated tokens/week for the checkout assistant (averaging ~1.1M tokens/day across US/EU).
- Embeddings usage for search/rerank projected small initially (~20k embeddings/week).
- Primary objectives: validate latency across region, monitor per-conversation cost uplift, and confirm quality when using 8-bit quantized model.

Cost / unit economics we discussed
- Target unit economics you mentioned: ~$1,000 per 1M generated tokens as the upper bound.
- With an expected steady-state of 3M tokens/week, that maps to ~$3k/week or ~$12k/month at that target.
- We discussed options to reduce unit cost (batching conversational prompts, prefix caching for repeat flows, and a lower-cost model variant for low-criticality responses).

Pilot credit/extension ask
- You asked for runway through the first 3 weeks of Jan while you ramp validation tests and secure internal budget.

What I can do now (proposed)
- I can approve a one-time top-up of $5,000 in trial credits to cover immediate burn through Jan 10. This is conditional on the pilot usage tracker and a checkpoint call on Jan 9.
- Dev (CC) will add quick batching + cache recommendations by EOD tomorrow to help stretch those credits.

Next steps (action owners / dates)

- Dev Patel (Redwood SE): provide batching/quantization recommendations & estimated cost delta (Due: Tue 12/22)

Hi all — following up with the technical notes I promised. Quick TL;DR and then a short checklist you can hand to your infra team: 

TL;DR: Best mix to hit ~$700/1M equivalent without impacting critical checkout prompts
- Model mix: route critical confirmations (payment auth, fraud-check prompts) to the higher-quality quantized 8-bit model (gpt-like-xl-q8) and non-critical assistant copy to a smaller 6B variant (gpt-lite-6b-q4).
- Batching: group callback-style assistant generation where safe — combine multi-turn prefill tokens into a single request when possible. Expect ~20-35% token reduction on conversation-heavy sessions.
- KV/prefix cache: enable a 24-hour prefix cache for repetitive session greetings/promotions — this reduces repeated prompt tokens for returning shoppers.
- Embeddings: compress vector stores for cold lookup (keep only 2 nearest neighbors for quick rerank) to save embedding units.

Checklist for BrightCart infra (copy/paste)
- Configure multi-model routing: gateway rule to route slot A -> gpt-like-xl-q8 and slot B -> gpt-lite-6b-q4 (example policy attached: seference-batch-recs.txt)
- Enable batch window of 40ms for non-interactive flows
- Turn on prefix KV caching for session keys with TTL 24h
- Monitor token burn by route and set alert at 70% credit consumption

Notes on monitoring & cost tracking
- Use the Redwood Console per-route breakdown; I’ll add a dashboard template to the Drive folder so you can see weekly token/route cost.

If you want, we can run a quick smoke test with a simulated peak hour load next week (I can coordinate with your SRE team).
